academics-and-cultural-commentators-clas.headline: Academics & Cultural Commentators - Class In British Film & TV
academics-and-cultural-commentators-clas.author: Tom M. Novak
academics-and-cultural-commentators-clas.core: Posted in last 7 days Academics & Cultural Commentators - Class In British Film & TV What counts as a good life on screen and who gets to have one? I’m writing a report on representations of class in British film and TV over the past two to three years: working-class lives, middle-class aspirations, and the ways stories shape our understanding of ambition, success and belonging. In The Cage, casino workers steal while juggling financial pressure and family responsibilities. In On Falling, a warehouse worker’s exhausting routine leaves little room for connection. What happens to the promise of a good life when working hard barely keeps you afloat? Getting ahead brings its own complications. California Schemin’ follows Scottish rappers adopting American identities to overcome industry prejudice. Dreaming Whilst Black uses comedy to explore creative ambition, awkward encounters and gatekeeping. How much of yourself must you edit before someone recognises your talent? But class also runs through the pleasures of everyday life: family banter, friendships, neighbourhood loyalties and the satisfaction of being understood. Scrapper gives estate life colour, imagination and tenderness. Comedy can turn familiar class assumptions into a shared joke—or make someone else’s background the punchline. I’m particularly interested in that balance: stories that acknowledge inequality while allowing characters humour, desire and joy. And stories where fulfilment might mean sustaining your relationships and community, rather than leaving them behind. I’d love to speak with academics, cultural commentators and media strategists working on these themes. It would be a 15–20-minute chat, and I’d welcome perspectives and examples that challenge this framing. Interested, or know someone I should speak to? Please comment or send me a message. #BritishTelevision #BritishFilm #SocialClass #PopularCulture #Comedy #CulturalInsights

teachers-and-school-leaders-lasting-chan.core: Posted in last 7 days Teachers & School Leaders - Lasting Change From Professional Learning If professional learning has had a lasting change for you? I want to speak to you. I’m exploring why and when it happens - but for real, I want to speak to real people and hear it warts and all. Not just a session you enjoyed, a course you completed or a day out of school that gave you some useful ideas, but an experience that genuinely changed something about how you work, how you see yourself as a professional, or what you believe you are capable of. From November, I’m beginning a collection of case studies exploring the lasting impact of professional learning, and I’m looking to speak to people who can reflect on an experience that made a difference to them. I’m interested in what people remember, what stayed with them, what they did differently afterwards, and how they know it made a difference. I’m equally interested in what didn’t work, what they struggled to apply, and what might have made the experience more meaningful. I’m deliberately not looking for a particular type of CPD, programme or course. It might have been a formal development programme, a conversation with a colleague, working alongside someone who challenged your thinking, or an experience that changed how you saw your place within the profession. I’m particularly interested in the relationship between professional learning, our sense of ourselves as professionals, our sense of belonging, and the impact we can see in our practice. I want to listen to people’s experiences and explore what we might learn from them about how professional learning really makes a difference. If you’ve had an experience of professional learning that you believe changed something for you, I’d ❤️ to hear from you. I’m hoping to begin conversations in November, and I’d be really grateful if you’d be willing to share your experience. Please comment below or send me a message if you’d be interested in taking part. What is it about that experience that has stayed with you?
